newsitem.title: JAPAN: Goods, services trade surplus unlikely to jump - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Goods, services trade surplus unlikely to jump - MOF.

text.p: Japan's surplus in the goods and services trade is unlikely to expand drastically, as Tokyo is putting utmost efforts into economic management led by domestic demand, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Wednesday.
"I see today's (current account) data as a short-term fluctuation," Mitsuzuka said.
"The surplus in the goods and services trade is unlikely to expand drastically, as we are putting utmost efforts into economic management led by domestic demand," he said.

"The increase in the surplus in May has been affected by special factors such as the increase in the consumption tax. We need to keep watch over future movements to determine whether there has been a change in the declining trend of the surplus," he said.
He said the effect of the rise in the sales tax was temporary, although it was hard to determine without enough data how long this effect would linger.

Asked about the indictment on Wednesday of former Nomura Securities Co Ltd president Hideo Sakamaki, Mitsuzuka said: "We will receive a recommendation from the SESC (Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission). After that we will deal with it (the company) severely."
Tokyo prosecutors said earlier on Wednesday they had indicted Sakamaki on charges of paying 320 million yen to "sokaiya" racketeer Ryuichi Koike.
They said Nomura itself had also been indicted on charges of violating Japan's Securities and Exchange Law, as had former managing director Nobutaka Fujikura.
Prosecutors said in a statement that Sakamaki and Fujikura had conspired with other Nomura officials to pay 320 million yen in cash to Koike around March 24, 1995.
They said the cash was paid in exchange for assurances from Koike that proceedings at a Nomura shareholders' meeting on June 29, 1995, would go smoothly.
